description: A seven-panel composite figure of low-density steel microstructures. Panels (a)-(f) are grey-scale optical micrographs of three alloys; the seventh is a colour-coded orientation map. (a) 100 µm scale bar, labelled (a): equiaxed austenite grains with straight annealing twins and sparse dark particles — essentially single phase. (b) 50 µm scale bar: equiaxed grains crossed by numerous straight parallel bands/twin plates and dark particles. (c) 100 µm scale bar, annotated "Grey: γ / White: B2": bright white second-phase particles decorate grain boundaries and grain interiors of the grey γ matrix. (d) 50 µm scale bar: same two-phase structure, with coarser white particles and some elongated ones. (e) 100 µm scale bar: a distinctly different, dark interdendritic network with bright second phase between the dendrite arms. (f) 50 µm scale bar: long bright stringers of B2 elongated along the rolling direction (vertical), the most strongly aligned stringers of the set. The final colour panel (also labelled (a)) is an EBSD inverse-pole-figure orientation map, 50 µm scale bar, showing many differently coloured, partly elongated grains with no dominant orientation colouring. No composition, temperature or phase-fraction values are printed on any panel, and the caption's panel (g) XRD patterns are not present in the supplied images.

subfigures.description: Grey-scale optical micrograph, 100 µm scale bar. Equiaxed grains with straight annealing twins, clean grain boundaries and a few small dark particles; apparently a single-phase austenitic structure.
Grey-scale optical micrograph, 50 µm scale bar. Equiaxed grains traversed by abundant straight, parallel thin bands (twin/slip plates) plus dark particles; no clear second-phase stringers.
Grey-scale optical micrograph, 100 µm scale bar, annotated 'Grey: γ' and 'White: B2'. Grey matrix grains outlined by bright white B2 particles along boundaries and inside grains.
Grey-scale optical micrograph, 50 µm scale bar. Equiaxed grains with white B2 particles at boundaries and interiors; a few coarser, slightly elongated white particles.
Grey-scale optical micrograph, 100 µm scale bar. Dark, interdendritic/cellular pattern with a bright continuous second-phase network between dark regions; visually distinct from (c) and (d).

Grey-scale optical micrograph, 50 µm scale bar. Long bright stringers aligned vertically (rolling direction) in a darker matrix with equiaxed grains between them; stringers are thicker and more continuous than in (d).

Colour EBSD inverse-pole-figure orientation map, 50 µm scale bar, built from many individually coloured grains of varied size, some elongated; no orientation-colour legend or axes are visible. Its label and modality do not match the caption's description of panel (a).

observations.observation: The group contains six grey-scale optical micrographs (labelled (a)-(f)) plus one colour EBSD orientation map; scale bars are 100 µm in (a), (c), (e) and 50 µm in (b), (d), (f) and the colour map.
Panel (c) carries the printed legend 'Grey: γ' and 'White: B2', identifying the grey matrix as austenite and the bright white second phase as B2.
Panel (a) shows a largely single-phase equiaxed austenite structure with straight annealing twins and no visible white second phase.
Panel (e) shows a dark interdendritic pattern with a bright second-phase network, a morphology clearly different from the grain-boundary-particle morphology seen in (c) and (d).
Panel (f) contains long bright stringers aligned parallel to the vertical direction of the image (rolling direction), more continuous than the dispersed particles in (d).

The colour map panel shows numerous differently coloured grains with no dominant orientation colour and no visible legend or axes; it is labelled (a), which conflicts with the caption's identification of (a) as an optical micrograph of 28Mn0Ni.
No XRD pattern panel is present among the supplied images, although the caption lists '(g) XRD patterns of the hot-rolled alloys'.
The caption assigns (a, b) to 28Mn0Ni, (c, d) to 28Mn5Ni and (e, f) to 15Mn5Ni, the first of each pair being as-cast plus homogenised and the second hot-rolled.
The citing text states that the Ni-containing alloys (28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni) consist of two phases whereas 28Mn0Ni is primarily single phase.

The citing text states that in the hot-rolled alloys the B2 phase exists both as polygonal particles and as elongated stringers along the rolling direction, matching the morphology seen in (d) and especially (f).
The citing text states that 15Mn5Ni contains a relatively higher volume fraction of B2 phase than 28Mn5Ni, indicating B2 formation is favoured at lower Mn content.

The citing text states that the B2 fraction decreased slightly on hot rolling at 1323 K, e.g. 15Mn5Ni dropping from ~15% (as-cast) to ~12% (hot-rolled); no such percentage is printed in any panel of this figure.
